text:
sam: quick request — can someone run a focused throughput + latency bench on staging? We've seen intermittent 200–700ms tail spikes when a flood of small requests (<=64 tokens) hit a single shard. suspect continuous-batching fallback path + max_batch_size interactions. want a small matrix: varying max_batch_size (8, 16, 32), batching_window_ms (5, 20), and max_tokens_per_request (64, 128). add KV-cache cold vs warm run. need raw p95/p99 and per-token cost. reply if you can take it.

maya: I can take this today. do you want the runs against the current canary (runtime/pr/421) or the mainline? also, does this include the new queue-priority patch?

sam: thanks @maya — run against canary (runtime/pr/421) *with* and *without* queue-priority enabled. that's the suspected vector. please tag results to the thread.

ryan: can you paste the exact perf-runner command you want? i can wrap it in CI job if helpful.

sam: sure — something like:
```
perf-runner bench --env staging --model redwood-7b-v1 --concurrency 200 \  --seq-len 64 --payload-size 64 \  --max-batch-size 16 --batch-window-ms 20 \  --kv-cache warm --duration 5m --out ./artifacts/run-1799001111
```
run for each combo, and for smaller batch sizes reduce concurrency to keep queue occupancy realistic.

alex: FYI i pushed a small logging tweak to the canary that prints batch composition (ids, sizes) to staged logs — should help diagnose fallback churn. link: https://git.internal/r/redwood/runtime/commit/9f3e

maya: starting runs now. i'll run (8,16,32) x (5,20) x (64,128) with kv-cache warm/cold. estimated 12 runs, ~1hr total. logging to s3: s3://redwood-perf/staging/1799001111/

jen: heads-up from eng-sre: staging has one node with degraded NIC — might bias latency. recommend excluding node-staging-07. i'll cordon it for the window if you want.

maya: please cordon it @jen — i'll re-run if any noisy host appears.

alex: small heuristic to watch: when batch sizes are forced small the CPU spin on queue pop increases syscall rates -> I/O latencies show up at tail if NIC is noisy. that matches.

maya: first two runs done (max_batch=8, window=5ms, seq=64, kv=cold). p95=120ms, p99=420ms, mean per-token cost ~0.00032. uploading artifacts now.

maya: run results summary (s3://redwood-perf/staging/1799001111/summary.csv) — notable: enabling queue-priority reduced p99 by ~150ms for batch=8, but for batch>=32 p99 is stable ~95ms regardless.

perf-bot: auto-report: run-1799001111-1 completed. metrics attached. anomalies detected: p99 spike > 300ms in some cold-kv runs. See /artifacts/run-1799001111/packets.json

ryan: thanks @maya — can you attach the batch-composition logs alex added? want to verify whether fallback happened because of max tokens per batch or because of timeouts.

maya: attached tail of batch log:
```
[2026-03-17T10:12:04Z] batch_id=901 size=3 timeout_ms=6 requests=[r12,r13,r14] fallback=false
[2026-03-17T10:12:04Z] batch_id=902 size=1 timeout_ms=6 requests=[r15] fallback=true reason=queue_timeout
```
looks like queue_timeout triggered fallback for singletons during bursts.

alex: ok that points to batching_window_ms being too short for our arrival rate. increasing to 20ms should let batches form. but watch latency for individual small realtime requests.

maya: re-run with batch_window=20ms for the same combos. queued. ETA ~40m.

qa-bot: test plan linked: https://docs.internal/qa/perf-cases#cb-fallback — smoke checks included for correctness and regression.

maya: second wave done. summary: when window=20ms and max_batch>=16 p99 drops to <120ms across warm/cold KV. Singleton fallback events ~80% lower. cost delta +~3% due to slightly higher token latency but much better tail.

jen: with cordon in place, NIC noise is gone. re-run results look consistent. i'll keep the cordon until you merge a config tweak.

ryan: sounds like a safe default: set batching_window_ms=20 for small-token workloads and keep max_batch default 16. can we gate behind a feature flag (runtime.config.use_aggressive_window) so we can roll back?

sam: yes please add the flag. @ryan can you open a tiny config PR that flips window to 20 for the small-token profile and adds the FF? label it perf/rollback.

ryan: on it — PR: https://git.internal/r/redwood/runtime/pull/433. includes tests and rollout plan (canary 10% -> 50% -> 100% with automatic p99 guardrails).

alex: one more note: kv-cache cold runs still show occasional p99 > 300ms; looks like cache population adds jitter. suggest we prime shared KV-cache for hot prefixes in the scheduler if workload uses small repeated prefixes. i'll open a follow-up RFC.

maya: uploading final artifact bundle: s3://redwood-perf/staging/1799001111/final.tar.gz — includes perf csv, logs, batch-composition, flamegraphs.

perf-bot: summary card: p95 baseline(5ms window, batch=8)=118ms -> new default(20ms window, batch=16)=94ms; p99 baseline=420ms -> new=110ms. cost change +2.9%.

sam: awesome work everyone. next steps: 1) @ryan merge PR 433 behind FF, 2) @jen coordinate canary rollout + keep cordon for first hour, 3) @alex open RFC for KV priming, 4) @maya add the run artifacts to the perf dashboard and pin to the issue. i'll own tracking and send a short note to product about tradeoffs. closing this thread — will reopen if any regressions on canary. :thumbsup:
